findings.title: Admin-or-owner recipe lets an admin seize document ownership
findings.description: The copyable admin-or-owner update predicate authorizes an admin without requiring `@newData.ownerId == @data.ownerId`. An admin can therefore update `ownerId` to itself or an accomplice and subsequently exercise permissions reserved for the owner, such as owner-gated reads or deletes. Although the page later gives general immutable-field advice, the concrete ownership recipe does not apply that protection and is unsafe when copied as written.
findings.recommendation: Preserve ownership specifically on the admin branch. If owners may transfer, use a rule shaped like `@user.id != null && ((@data.ownerId == @user.id) || (get(/admins/@user.id) != null && @newData.ownerId == @data.ownerId))`. If transfers are not required, preserve ownerId for every update.
